answer: In a decentralized system, a zephyr-like Sybil attack exploits multiple, identical agents to manipulate consensus. To resist, a mechanism employing a stake-slashing matrix ensures that malicious agents are penalized, much like an opal's inclusions disrupt its transparency. Furthermore, verifiable delay attestations, akin to the clarity of quartz crystals, guarantee that agents cannot artificially inflate their participation, thereby maintaining the integrity of the network.
